messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: High error rate (502/504) and elevated tail latency on /v1/embeddings - affected customers: dedicated pool eu-west-1 (pgp-dedicated-12). Paging primary oncall.

Maya: I'm on it — looking at the serving pool metrics.

Sam: seeing kv-cache misses spike and a cascade of CPU steal on node g3-12. Rolling errors started at 02:02 UTC.

Devin: Confirmed. Replayed request logs, request sizes consistent. Looks like background compaction/GC on that instance correlated with latency spikes.

Maya: I'm throttling new session allocations to that pool and shifting routing to fallback variant model: text-embed-compact-v2. Doing graceful drain of 3 instances.

Priya: Noted. Customer impact: two enterprise customers had retries increase and some request timeouts. Support ticket numbers: SUP-6682, SUP-6685.

Jorge: Adding quick mitigation: increase prefix-KV cache TTL for embeddings in the fallback route to reduce backend load. Patch applied in console (UI) and will take ~30s to propagate.

Devin: Patch propagated. Errors dropping but still elevated p95. Draining has freed up memory on one node.

Maya: primary->secondary handoff in 25m for on-call rotation. I'll keep the channel live for the handoff notes.

incident-bot: Deployment bot: canary rollback initiated for commit ab3f2c6 to stable on pool pgp-dedicated-12 by Maya at 02:15 UTC.

Sam: Rollback complete, monitoring. p99 latency back to normal range for most traffic.

Priya: Support update draft: "We experienced degraded embeddings throughput in eu-west-1 between 02:02 and 02:48 UTC due to a node-level resource contention event. We've routed traffic to fallback model and rolled back a recent change; persistent errors resolved at 02:48 UTC. Ops continues postmortem and will follow up on SLA/billing." Thoughts? :thumbsup:

Maya: LGTM. Add note that two customers with reserved capacity may qualify for SLA credits — I'll attach usage windows.

Jorge: Running an automated health check across the pool now. Also filing infra issue about compaction scheduling on these instance types.

Devin: Quick command I used to inspect the KV cache metrics:
```
kubectl exec -n inference svc/kv-metrics -- curl http://localhost:8080/metrics | grep prefix_cache_miss
```
Gave immediate signal that miss-rate rose 8x around incident start.

Maya: Postmortem plan: bone-up timeline, root cause hypothesis (compaction + a recent kernel update interaction), remediation (disable compaction during high-traffic windows, improve scheduling), and targeted tests. Who can own the writeup?

Sam: I'll own initial draft of postmortem (TL;DR + timeline + mitigation). Will sync with Devin for technical root cause and Jorge for infra action items.

Priya: Schedule postmortem review meeting: proposed 2026-03-18 15:00 UTC. Pinged interested parties.

Maya: Assign action items here — keep as simple strings so we can track: 1) Disable compaction window until fix (owner: Jorge, due: 2026-03-20). 2) Add compaction + kernel interaction test (owner: Devin, due: 2026-04-02). 3) Update routing fallback docs and add runbook step (owner: Sam, due: 2026-03-25).

Jorge: I put a short-term patch to avoid concurrent compaction on the same host; will bake a more complete scheduler.

Priya: Support/customer comms schedule: first update posted. Follow-up email to impacted customers with postmortem + SLA credit offer after finance confirms amounts.

Maya: Elaine (Finance) — can you advise on SLA credit process for two reserved customers? We need estimated pro-rated credits for 46m of partial degradation (02:02 - 02:48 UTC) for customers with committed capacity.

Elaine (Finance): I can run the calc. Need: customer IDs, committed monthly amount, and the SLA definition (downtime vs degraded throughput). If you can paste customer IDs and bound of impact (full outage vs degraded), I'll compute pro-rated credit and draft adjustment entries.

Priya: Customers: RED-2483 and RED-2519. Both were on Reserved Dedicated Bronze plan. Impact: degraded throughput and increased errors (timeouts) but not a hard outage. We'll include per-minute error rates and the window 02:02-02:48 UTC in the postmortem.

Maya: Attaching quick numbers: RED-2483 had 3.1k tokens/min during window; RED-2519 had 1.8k. Both saw ~12% request failure and 40% higher tail latency.

Elaine (Finance): Thanks. I'll treat this as "degraded service" per SLA clause 4.2 — credits are pro-rated by affected minutes weighted by severity band (partial outage = 50% credit of per-minute rate). I'll prepare a draft calculation and post adjustment lines to billing queue. Expect a preliminary number in 6-8 business hours.

billing-bot: Billing action queued: ACTION-9921 created for manual adjustment review (owner: Elaine).

Maya: Once Elaine posts numbers, I'll sign off on customer emails and coordinate the support team to issue credits. Also, can we please add a follow-up item in the postmortem to track credit issuance completion?

Sam: Added follow-up: "Confirm SLA credit issuance and update postmortem" (owner: Priya, due: 2026-03-22).

Devin: Final checks — logs retained, trace spans saved; if finance needs exact request IDs for audit we can provide filtered logs for the exact window.

Elaine (Finance): Posted preliminary credit estimates in the billing console (internal ticket BIL-3145) and emailed finance-ops. RED-2483: estimated credit $3,420; RED-2519: estimated credit $1,980 (subject to final approval).

Priya: Thanks Elaine. I'll update customer-facing templates and include those amounts as ranges until finalized.

Maya: Great work team. We'll reconvene in the scheduled postmortem meeting. Leaving this thread open for final billing confirmation and the action-item checklist. If anyone needs immediate follow-up, add a direct message to me. :heart:

incident-bot: RESOLVED: Incident closed by Maya at 02:48 UTC. Postmortem scheduled.
